To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic constriction injury of the sciatic nerves in the rat induces chronic pain and a decrease in the number of GAD-immunostained cells in the spinal cord dorsal horn, which is reversed by transplantation of 5HT-secreting cells.

chronic neuropathic hindlimb pain is ameliorated after transplantation of immortalized serotogenic cells into the lumbar spinal subarachnoidal space of rats, and the mechanism of this effect is likely related to the reversal of the induction of an endogenous dorsal horn pain mechanism.

transplants of 5HT and 5HT/BDNF-producing cells, but not 5HT-negative cells, reverse the induction and expression of chronic neuropathic tactile and thermal pain, and the changes in GABA- and glutamate decarboxyase-immunoreactive cell numbers in the lumbar dorsal horn, induced by CCI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of chronic pain, particularly the role of 5HT and GABA in the spinal cord.
the development of a bioengineered cell replacement strategy for treating chronic pain, which is the most prevalent cause of chronic disability in the United States.
the development of bioengineered neuronal cell transplants for treatment of chronic pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transplanted 46A-B cells, which synthesize 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin, 5HT), reverse the induction of neuropathic pain by reversing the decrease in GAD and increase in GABA- containing neurons in the spinal dorsal horns.

transplanted 46A-B-14 cells reverse the induction of chronic pain and the associated alterations in the GABA-ergic system in the dorsal horn, and that this reversal is related to increased 5HT synthesis and perhaps BDNFB production by these cells.

transplants of 5HT-producing cells into the subarached space of the lumbo-spinal cord after nerve injury can alleviate neuropathic pain and can reverse the induction of an endogenous spinal pain mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transplants of RN46A cells reverse neuropathic pain and the changes in GABAergic neurons in the dorsal horn, and that these transplants may have potential as a treatment for chronic pain.

the transplants of RN46A cells expressing BDNF and secreting 5HT, but not 46A-VI control cells, ameliorated neuropathic pain by reversing the changes in GAD- or GABA-immunoreactive cell numbers in the lumbar dorsal horn.

the transplantation of 46A cells into the subarachednoid space can alleviate chronic pain, and that the mechanism of this alleviation is related to a decrease in GABA synthesis and a decrease in the number of GAD and GABA immunoreactive cells in the dorsal horn.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the RN46A cell line can be used to promote the recovery from chronic pain and that the mechanism of recovery may involve the reversal of the induction of GABAergic inhibition in the spinal dorsal cord.
the RN46A cell line is an excellent tool to investigate the mechanisms by which serotonergic neurons modulate pain.

transplant of bioengineerered 5HT neurons into the lumbar subarachnold space of the rat spinal cord can ameliorate neuropathic pain induced by nerve injury, and that the mechanism of pain reduction involves a reversal in the induction and maintenance mechanism of an endogenous dorsal horn mechanism of pain, likely involving changes in GAD and GABA.
